title: Geology of the Charleston phosphate area, South Carolina
citation: Malde, H.E., 1959, Geology of the Charleston phosphate area, South Carolina: U.S. Geological Survey Bulletin 1079, map scale 1:24,000.
notes: Pages 1-5 are OCR of the map plates and are heavily garbled; only the legible explanation text of plate 1 was used, and unit symbols read as Qif/Qip in the OCR are recorded as Qlf/Qlp (inferred). Plate 1 assigns no unit names to the two youngest sand descriptions except 'Terrace deposits along Goose Creek' and 'Sand on Tenmile Hill'; the middle description is attributed to the Pamlico formation by inference from page 15. Ladson formation maximum thickness: plate 1 says 33 feet, the abstract (page 15) says 35 feet; both recorded. Logs on pages 25, 41 and 48 give bed thicknesses, not depths; thicknesses are put in interval notes rather than converted to depths. The type-section auger hole number is garbled ('2^2') and recorded as 242 from figure 5 (inferred). Fossil tables on pages 27-28 and 42-43 are garbled and were not itemized.
